title: Billing variance governance and crediting SOP
author: Marcus Nguyen
body:
Overview:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) describes governance, tooling, and decision rules for investigating billing variances between measured usage and invoiced amounts, and for issuing credits or adjustments. It covers scheduled monthly checks, event-driven investigations, entitlement/tier corrections, journalization for revenue accounting, and customer communications. The SOP emphasizes reproducibility, minimal customer disruption, and clear audit trails.

Applicability:
- Applies to hosted API customers, embedding units, and Dedicated/Reserved capacity tenants billed via our billing pipeline.
- Does not apply to professional services or non-recurring custom invoices handled by Contracts.

Primary objectives:
- Detect billing mismatches within the first 5 business days after invoice generation.
- Resolve low-risk variances automatically or within 7 business days.
- Escalate material variances to Finance leadership and Legal as appropriate.
- Ensure every credit is traceable to evidence and recorded in revenue systems within the same accounting period where possible.

Key roles and contacts:
- Billing Operations (primary owner): issue credits, maintain reconciliation ledger, perform accounting entries. Email: billing-ops@redwood.com
- Billing Engineering: develop and maintain reconciliation queries and automation. Slack: #billing-svc
- Customer Success (CS): notify customers and manage communications. Email: cs-escalations@redwood.com
- Legal: review contract exceptions or disallowed-credits clauses.
- Audit & Compliance: retain evidence bundles and respond to external auditor requests.

Data sources and artifacts (summary):
- Measured usage feed: canonical event stream (Snowflake table billing_events) containing customer_id, event_ts, token_count, request_id, model_tag.
- Invoice records: billing system export (invoices_export) with invoice_id, billing_period, billed_amount, applied_adjustments.
- Operational telemetry: request logs, retry counts, and edge-proxy incident markers.
- Reconciliation report: daily_variances table containing computed delta metrics and flags used for triage.

Routine monthly reconciliation process (stepwise):
1) Run automated snapshot (Day 0 = invoice date + 1): capture usage and invoice snapshots to the reconciliation schema.
2) Compute deltas (Day 0): per-customer delta = measured_usage_units - billed_units. Attach preliminary reason codes using heuristic rules (duplication, tiered-pricing mismatch, proration, rounding).
3) Auto-dismiss small deltas (Day 0): automatically close deltas that are less than 0.5% of billed amount or under $25 USD, with an audit marker.
4) Auto-correct deterministic errors (Day 1): apply algorithmic fixes for known issues (legacy multiplier, timezone misalignment). Record entries in reconciliation_corrections with references to the code change and query ids.
5) FinanceOps review (Day 2	6): FinanceOps triages remaining items and approves credits up to the low-risk threshold.
6) Multi-team review (Day 2	6): Items above the low-risk threshold require a triage meeting with Billing Eng and CS within 3 business days.
7) Legal review (as needed): if contract language or marketplace flows restrict crediting, escalate to Legal.
8) Issue adjustment and record (Day 5	6): create credit memo, update invoice record, and post contra-revenue entry in the RevRec ledger.
9) Communicate to customer (Day 5): CS sends templated notification with explanation, amount, and how the credit appears on their account.

Decision thresholds and authorization matrix:
- Low-risk auto-approval: credits <= $2,000 and no disputed technical cause. Authorized: FinanceOps on behalf of Head of Finance.
- Mid-risk escalation: $2,001 to $25,000 requires joint approval from FinanceOps and Billing Eng.
- High-risk/contractual: > $25,000 or when contract terms constrain credits requires Head of Finance and Legal sign-off.

Common reason codes and handling patterns:
- DUPLICATE_EVENTS: caused by telemetry replay; credit full attributable amount after SRE confirms duplication. Evidence: log IDs and replay markers.
- TIER_PRICING_MISMATCH: customer was billed at incorrect tier; compute delta using contract schedule and prorate for the period.
- PRORATION_ERROR: mid-cycle plan change misapplied; compute daily prorata using days_in_period.
- ROUNDED_UNIT: rounding differences due to aggregation windows; credit only when amount exceeds rounding tolerance and is customer-impacting.

Audit and accounting requirements:
- Each credit must include: unique reconciliation_ticket_id, list of evidence links (Snowflake query URLs or S3 object paths), approver name(s), credit memo id, accounting batch id, and timestamp.
- Retain the full bundle of evidence and ticket notes for 7 years in the compliance S3 path.
- All contra-revenue entries must reference the original revenue recognition ledger line and include an explanation for auditors.

Operational tooling and runbooks (links):
- Reconciliation jobs: airflow/dags/reconciliation_v3 (runbook available).
- Key queries: queries/reconciliation/compute_daily_delta.sql (Snowflake).
- Manual adjustment UI: FinanceOps Console -> Credits -> Create Adjustment.

Metrics and reporting (monthly):
- Variance volume (count of tickets). Target: decline 10% QoQ.
- Variance dollar total as percent of billed revenue. Target: <= 0.4%.
- Mean days to closure. Target: <= 6 business days.

Escalation examples and templates:
- Example escalation: if an SRE incident caused a 20% uptick in duplicate events and total variance exceeds $10k, Billing Eng opens incident ticket, FinanceOps pauses auto-approval, and Legal is informed for material customer exposures.
- Customer communication template: "We identified an overbilling on invoice [#], we have applied a credit of [amount]. See attached breakdown."

Edge cases and guidance:
- Marketplace/reseller transactions: do not issue credits unilaterally on reseller invoices. Coordinate with Partner Ops and the reseller to agree adjustments.
- Contracts with "no-credit" clauses: route to Legal; only Legal can approve exceptions and must produce signed exception memo.
- Retrospective corrections spanning closed accounting periods: engage Accounting and Audit to determine acceptable treatment (journal vs. credit memo).

Change control and review cadence:
- FinanceOps and Billing Engineering must review this SOP quarterly and sign off on any changes to thresholds or automation logic.
- Major changes must be approved by Head of Finance and documented in the change log.

Appendix A	6 Suggested fields for reconciliation ticket (minimum):
- ticket_id
- customer_id
- billing_period
- detected_delta_amount
- reason_code
- evidence_links
- proposed_credit_amount
- approver_ids
- credit_memo_id

Appendix B	6 Quick checklist for FinanceOps when issuing a credit:
1) Confirm evidence links resolve to reproducible queries or CSVs.
2) Verify approver scope for credit amount.
3) Create credit memo and record ID in ticket.
4) Post contra-revenue entry and update RevRec linkage.
5) Notify CS and attach customer-facing explanation.
6) Close ticket and archive audit bundle.

Document history:
- 2029-03-05: Created by Marcus Nguyen
- 2029-03-12: Thresholds and automation details updated after Billing Eng review

End of SOP.
